ops.body:
Banked derivables from the cc-notes v0.21.0 migration lane, parked 2026-08-03
because `internal/helperdeployment` cannot compile until fusekit tags v1.16.0.
This note is the work order for the resumed lane. Everything below was derived
by running code, not by reading it.

## Why the lane parked

`internal/helperdeployment` was planned as the "daemonkit-only half". It is not.
It imports `fusekit/holder`, `mountproto`, `mountservice`, `transportproto`, and
`trustroles`, and `fusekit@v1.15.4/holder` itself imports NINE deleted daemonkit
packages: bundle, codeidentity, daemon, deployment, proc, service, trust, wire,
worker. `fusekit/fuset` imports three more (proc, trust, worker). Go compiles per
package, so nothing in helperdeployment can compile or run until fusekit tags —
which means `makeDeploymentPolicyDigest()` cannot be executed and the golden
digest cannot be re-derived by running it.

Held packages (8), all fusekit-reachable, none fixable without the fusekit tag:
cmd/cc-notes, cmd/cc-notes-helper-package, internal/cli, internal/fusefs,
internal/helperapp, internal/helperclient, internal/helperdeployment,
internal/helperpackage.

## 1. The seven-item daemonkit-attributable policy delta

Apply exactly these to `deploymentPolicy` in
`internal/helperdeployment/deployment_identity.go`. Nothing else in the struct
changes for daemonkit reasons.

1. DELETE `service.session_type` (was `0`) — `launchd.Agent` has no successor field.
2. DELETE `service.process_type` (was `0`) — same.
3. DELETE `service.quiesce.stop_role` (was `"fusekit.stop-controller.v1"`).
4. DELETE `service.quiesce.receipt_role` (was `"fusekit.receipt-controller.v1"`).
5. DELETE `service.quiesce.readiness_role` (was `"fusekit.readiness-controller.v1"`).
6. DELETE `service.quiesce.require_daemonkit_stop_receipt` (was `true`).
7. CHANGE `runtime.state.runtime_policy_digest`:
   `c18ba0b41ea91be2d3d154740c2806a053bcbb1b8ef20e495f5b95cfe0c2272d`
   -> `7c6cb501a79e904ab8793b315d351d02a0d0c62f6b24683bafd92de03ea2eb2e`

Items 3-5 delete the `fusekit/trustroles` import from the policy — the only
fusekit dependency the rewrite removes.

`service.restart_policy` is a pure TYPE swap with NO JSON delta:
`service.RestartAlways` and `launchd.RestartAlways` are both `1`.

## 2. Golden digest: reproduced, and the provisional successor

The current pinned golden at `deployment_identity_test.go:136` is
`8418f2c021f7d4bb1733d3b298ec32fb95caefd11644bb2c64d2bd382e1e54ac`.

REPRODUCED EXACTLY on 2026-08-03: reverted go.mod to daemonkit v0.20.9, dumped
`deploymentPolicyJSON()` from a temporary in-package test, sha256 of the payload
matched the pinned golden byte for byte. That validates the baseline below.

A Python re-serializer was then proven byte-identical to Go's `json.Marshal`
output (same bytes, same digest), so field edits could be applied without Go.
The recipe: `json.dumps(separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False)` then escape
`<`, `>`, `&` as `\u003c`, `\u003e`, `\u0026`.

Applying only the seven items above yields:

  PROVISIONAL DIGEST 726bce296a979704638569e7fed1d8abf51e44d904dc4b50080804863b929780

DO NOT PIN THIS VALUE. It is conditional on fusekit v1.15.4's constants. These
policy inputs are fusekit-pinned and must be re-read after the v1.16.0 tag:

- `protocols.wire_build` — HIGHEST RISK. Currently
  `"com.yasyf.fusekit.transport/18070c4dfd72029630be002151da16cc37cb9b1e44f3045ce31f079d3813029e/v1"`,
  a digest of fusekit's own transport, which the daemonkit-wire/G-frame work replaces.
- `protocols.mount_protocol`, `runtime_protocol`, `wire_protocol` (all `1` today).
- Every `runtime.native.fuse.*` value (the `holder.FUSE*` constants).
- `runtime.readiness.startup/settlement/observation_timeout_ns`
  (`holder.StandardReadinessContract()`).
- The `mountproto` enum strings: `required_phase`, `filesystem`, `required_state`,
  `required_step`, `required_error_code`, `required_broker_phase`.

Procedure for the resumed lane: repin fusekit, apply the seven items, run the
digest computation for real, and confirm the only differences from
`726bce29...` trace to fusekit-pinned inputs.

## 3. The requirement-digest algorithm changed (daemonkit-side, derivable now)

This is why item 7 exists, and it is easy to miss.

- v0.20.9 `trust.Requirement.ValidationDigest() (codeidentity.PolicyDigest, error)`
  hashed: TeamID, SigningIdentifier, then sorted entitlement requirements.
- v0.21.0 `daemonkit.Requirement.Digest() PolicyDigest` additionally covers
  `RequiredAppGroup`, a `binary.BigEndian` uint64 key-count prefix over the
  entitlement keys, and `AllowJIT`. It is also infallible (no error return).

The TYPE changed too: `codeidentity.PolicyDigest [32]byte` -> `daemonkit.PolicyDigest string`
(a hex string, `requirement.go:120`). So the `plan.go:51` swap is NOT the
value-type no-op the migration plan implies:

    hex.EncodeToString(runtimePolicy[:])   ->   string(runtimePolicy)

Recomputed against real v0.21.0 for cc-notes' requirement
(`TeamID: "SXKCTF23Q2"`, `SigningIdentifier: "com.yasyf.cc-notes.helper"`):
`7c6cb501a79e904ab8793b315d351d02a0d0c62f6b24683bafd92de03ea2eb2e`.

## 4. Designated requirement: NO REV NEEDED (verified)

v0.21 `deploy.designatedRequirement` (deploy/deploy.go:596, unexported)
delegates to `internal/trust.Requirement.DRString()`, which renders:

    identifier "%s" and anchor apple generic and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "%s" and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] exists and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] exists

That is BYTE-IDENTICAL to what `helper-app/prepare-release.sh:8` already carries.
The migration plan's conditional ("if daemonkit's DR rendering differs from the
old DRString, the script revs too") resolves to: the script does NOT rev.

The only change needed is in `release_contract_test.go:241` — replace the
`trust.Requirement{...}.DRString()` computation with the literal string, since
root `Requirement` exports only `Digest`.

## 5. Source-text tripwire inventory — FIVE, not three

No compiler finds any of these. Land each rewrite in the same commit as its target.

1. `internal/helperapp/release_contract_test.go:146`
   `TestHelperDeploymentUsesDaemonkitSchemaOneState`. BIGGER than the plan's
   "146-199" suggests: 22 `assertFileContains` fragments over `deployment.go`
   (every one dead after the rewrite), 12 `assertFileExcludes` fragments, PLUS
   separate fragment sets over `internal/helperdeployment/deployment_identity.go`
   and `cmd/cc-notes-helper/main.go`.
2. `internal/helperapp/release_contract_test.go:241`
   `TestReleasePinsExactHelperDesignatedRequirement`. See section 4.
3. `internal/helperapp/release_contract_test.go:260`
   `TestOrdinaryCLIHasNoHelperChildDispatch`. Forbids `RunHelperChild`,
   `holder.RunChild`, `--fusekit-`. Daemonkit-neutral; SURVIVES UNCHANGED.
4. `internal/helperapp/release_contract_test.go:272`
   `TestActiveTreeHasNoRetiredHelperDeliverySurface`. THE FOURTH TRIPWIRE, and
   the one most easily missed: a tree-wide forbidden-string sweep
   (`assertTreeExcludes`) across 14 roots including `internal/`, `.github/`,
   `docs/`, `helper-app/`, `cmd/`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md`.
   Today it forbids only `daemonkit/fetch` and `.daemonkit-fetch`. This is where
   the eight now-deleted `daemonkit/*` import paths belong once the migration
   lands, so a stale import can never reappear.
5. `internal/homeguard/contract_test.go:50` — the `rootDeps` pin. See section 6.

## 6. homeguard rootDeps: paths AND launchd (both required)

`internal/homeguard/contract_test.go:50` pinned `github.com/yasyf/daemonkit/service`.
The v0.21 replacement is TWO paths, not one:

    "github.com/yasyf/daemonkit/paths"
    "github.com/yasyf/daemonkit/launchd"

Reasoning, verified against daemonkit's own dependency graph with `go list -deps`:

- The root `daemonkit` package and `deploy` both reach `daemonkit/paths`
  (the passwd-resolved state root).
- `daemonkit/launchd` reaches its home root via `internal/realhome` and does
  NOT reach `paths`. So pinning `paths` alone would miss any package importing
  only `launchd` — which writes `~/Library/LaunchAgents`.
- `daemonkit/durable` derives no home at all (deps: internal/flock only).

CAVEAT: this value is UNVERIFIED. `TestHomeDisciplineContract` shells out to a
module-wide `go list -test -json ./...`, which cannot resolve `internal/fusefs`
while fusekit is held, so the test bails before any subtest. The resumed lane
must run the guard and confirm.

## 7. HOME / DAEMONKIT_HOME audit — clean, and NOT a v0.21 regression

Audited all 37 sites (11 `t.Setenv("HOME")` across 8 files, 26 `"HOME="`
subprocess env lines across 5 files). VERDICT: all 37 stay; zero migrate.

- `internal/realhome` shipped in v0.20.9 too, with identical semantics: `Dir()`
  never reads HOME, honors `DAEMONKIT_HOME`, warns once via `slog.Warn`. The
  fleet-wide trap is "was this ever right", not "did v0.21 break it".
- cc-notes already solved it: `internal/homeguard/homeguard.go:64-86` package
  init redirects `CC_NOTES_HOME`, `DAEMONKIT_HOME`, and `HOME` to fresh temp
  dirs for every importing package. Proven live under the v0.21 pin: passwd home
  `/Users/yasyf`, `DAEMONKIT_HOME` a temp dir.
- All 11 `Setenv` sites sandbox cc-notes' OWN home derivation
  (`~/.cc-notes/helper-tools`, `~/Applications/CCNotesHelper.app`, `ccnhome.Root()`).
- 24 of 26 subprocess sites are inside homeguard's own tests; all 15 in
  `pins_test.go` are Go SOURCE-TEXT FIXTURES in AST-pin tables, not live envs.
- `internal/cli/e2e_test.go`'s `binEnv` (:46) builds from `os.Environ()` and
  appends, so `DAEMONKIT_HOME` rides through to the real-binary child.

RESIDUAL RISK for the resumed lane: `e2e_test.go:105` and `:379` assert
`res.Stderr == ""` for a real cc-notes child carrying `DAEMONKIT_HOME`. If any
exercised path reaches `realhome.Dir()`, daemonkit's `slog.Warn` lands on stderr
(daemonkit never configures the global logger, by design) and breaks the
invariant. Not firing today. cc-notes has NO log-level knob — grep for
`slog.SetDefault`, `SetLogLoggerLevel`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `LogLevel` across `cmd/`,
`internal/cli/`, `internal/ccnhome/` returns zero hits — so the usual mitigation
does not exist here and must be built.

## 8. Linux build preserved (landed 2026-08-03, verified)

cc-notes KEEPS its linux build; fleet repos run cc-notes record validation in
ubuntu CI jobs. The break was `internal/cli/editfile.go:16` (NO build tag)
importing `internal/fusefs`.

The clean fix was NOT an editfile split. `internal/fusefs/render.go` is pure Go
(stdlib + yaml + `internal/render` + `model`, zero daemonkit/fusekit) and holds
all ten functions editfile.go needs: RenderDoc, RenderNote, NewDocTemplate,
NewNoteTemplate, ParseDoc, ParseNote, DiffDoc, DiffNote, NewDoc, NewNote. Its own
package doc already said so: "Render, parse, diff, and the namespace model are
plain Go with no native filesystem dependency."

So `//go:build darwin` was added to exactly the EIGHT daemonkit/fusekit-reaching
non-test files: authority.go, business.go, git_driver.go, git_driver_mutation.go,
git_driver_registry.go, helper_runtime.go, provision_client.go, provisioning.go.
`editfile.go` is UNCHANGED, and linux keeps full `note add`/`doc add`/`edit`
behavior — no functionality lost, no fallback needed.

Verified: `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./cmd/cc-notes` GREEN
(valid static ELF x86-64). Darwin side still held on fusekit exactly as before;
the darwin green/held package split is byte-identical to pre-gate. Both CI
cross-compile steps kept.

KNOWN LATENT ITEM: `GOOS=linux go vet ./internal/fusefs` still fails on the nine
daemonkit-importing TEST files. Deliberately not tagged: `main_test.go` holds the
homeguard TestMain, and tagging it darwin would drop the home redirect for the
remaining linux tests — the exact home-discipline hole the guard exists to
prevent — and the guard cannot be run to verify while fusekit is held. No CI
impact: the test job runs on macOS and linux is build-only.

## 9. Worktree state at park

Worktree `/private/tmp/w2-cc-notes` (branch `w2-cc-notes`), NOT committed.
13 files modified: go.mod (daemonkit v0.20.9 -> v0.21.0), go.sum,
internal/helpercontract/provision.go (dropped `daemonkit/wire`;
`ProvisionRepositoryOperation wire.Op` -> untyped string const, since v0.21
`Business.Call(ctx, op string, body []byte)` takes a plain string and the tenant
param is gone — this moved the package HELD -> GREEN),
internal/homeguard/contract_test.go (section 6), the eight fusefs build tags
(section 8), and .github/workflows/ci.yml (test/lint/vuln ubuntu -> macos-latest;
helper was already macos; hook-tests/web/webui stay ubuntu).

fusekit pin deliberately left at v1.15.4.

Verification at park: 31 packages green, 8 held. `go test -race -count=1` over
the 30 testable green packages: 29 ok, 1 fail. The single failure is
`internal/homeguard` `TestHomeDisciplineContract`, blocked by the module-wide
`go list` (section 6), NOT by any edit in this lane.

TEST-RUNNER NOTE: `ulimit -u 2000` does NOT work on the dev box — roughly 2600
processes are already live for the uid, so every fork fails EAGAIN before any
test runs. Use `ulimit -u 4000` (soft cap 10666, hard 16000). cc-notes has no
`scripts/test.sh`; CI runs bare `go test -race ./...` on what is now a macOS
runner, which is the fork-storm shape AGENTS.md warns about. Adding a harness is
an open gap.

## 10. For the resumed lane (post fusekit v1.16.0)

- Repin fusekit, then re-derive the golden per section 2.
- Port helperdeployment onto `deploy` using
  `/private/tmp/w1-captain-hook/internal/hookd/deployment.go` as the template
  (if that worktree is gone, the shape is `deploy.Open(deploy.Config{App,
  Requirement, Daemon, Agents})` + Install/Supersede/Activate/Uninstall/Reset).
- Trust posture for the signed helper stays `ServingSigned` (owner decision).
- `daemonkit.NewGate`: CHECKED 2026-08-03, DOES NOT APPLY to cc-notes. NewGate
  exists for "a caller who must own the fork (creack/pty)" (adopt.go:66-71).
  cc-notes owns no fork: grepping `internal/helperclient/`, `internal/fusefs/`,
  and `cmd/cc-notes-helper/` for `os.Pipe`, `ExtraFiles`, `StartProcess`,
  `posix_spawn`, and pty returns ZERO hits. The two spawn surfaces are launchd
  (which owns the fork for the helper LaunchAgent) and `fuset.NewToolPool`
  (`internal/helperclient/fuse_tools.go:39`), which is FUSEKIT's own worker pool.
  So if a NewGate adoption is warranted anywhere here, it belongs in fusekit's
  lane, not cc-notes'.
- Watch the three known traps: the `MaxFrame`/`MaxDetail` pin (base64 + 4 KiB
  reserve means the real ceiling is ~75% of MaxFrame), `launchd.ErrNotOwned` on
  markerless v0.20 plists on uninstall-before-first-v0.21-install paths, and
  `Restart` stated explicitly.
